The Woods on Netflix: Everything We Know About the New Harlan Coben Thriller

Netflix is continuing its hugely successful partnership with bestselling thriller author Harlan Coben with a brand-new adaptation of The Woods. The upcoming British mystery series stars Tom Bateman and Michelle Keegan and is already generating excitement among fans of suspense television.

After the massive success of previous Harlan Coben adaptations like Fool Me Once, Stay Close, and Missing You, Netflix is once again bringing viewers a dark mystery packed with twists, emotional drama, and shocking secrets.

Tom Bateman and Michelle Keegan Lead The Woods

The new Netflix adaptation features a star-studded cast led by:

  • Tom Bateman (Based on a True Story)
  • Michelle Keegan (Fool Me Once)
  • Mandeep Dhillon (MobLand)
  • Pearce Quigley (Small Prophets)
  • Rade Sherbedgia (Slow Horses)

Additional cast members include:
James Buckley, Shannon Watson, Pamela Nomvete, Kerry Howard, Roger Barclay, Simon Lowe, Mila Moring, Dean Fagan, Tom Allen, Tracy-Ann Oberman, Charlotte Beaumont, Christopher Harper, Tre Jordan Holmes, Nicola Stephenson, Harry Goodson-Bevan, Joe Dolan, Thea Achillea, Flynn Allen, and Hannah McIver.

Michelle Keegan’s involvement is especially notable after Fool Me Once became one of Netflix’s most-watched shows of 2024.

What Is The Woods About?

The Woods centers on Paul “Cope” Copeland, played by Tom Bateman, a successful barrister and devoted single father haunted by a devastating tragedy from his past.

Twenty years earlier, Cope’s sister Camille disappeared from a summer camp under mysterious circumstances. The event destroyed his family and left unanswered questions that never truly disappeared.

When the body of a man connected to the original case is discovered decades later, Cope becomes convinced his sister may still be alive. As he searches for answers, he reunites with his former love Lucy Silverfield, played by Michelle Keegan.

Together, they uncover hidden lies, cover-ups, and long-buried family secrets that threaten to unravel everything Cope has built.

Fans can expect:

  • Psychological suspense
  • Emotional storytelling
  • Complex mysteries
  • Unexpected plot twists
  • Dark family secrets
  • High-stakes drama

The Creative Team Behind The Woods

Netflix is once again partnering with several key creatives behind previous Harlan Coben successes.

The series is being produced by Quay Street, led by acclaimed producer Nicola Shindler. Longtime Harlan Coben collaborator Danny Brocklehurst returns as writer and executive producer.

Writers

  • Danny Brocklehurst
  • Charlotte Coben
  • Tom Farrelly
  • Joe Forrest

Executive Producers

  • Harlan Coben
  • Nicola Shindler
  • Richard Fee

“The Woods is a haunting and very personal story. It has everything you expect from us — twisty, turning, gasp-inducing — but at the core is a story of old love and yearning.”

Who Are the Casting Directors Behind The Woods?

The casting team behind The Woods brings extensive experience in film and television production.

Nadia Lebik

  • Scarborn (2023)

Lebik has experience across casting and assistant directing, helping shape emotionally driven and suspense-focused productions.

Roman Candle Casting

The production is also working with Roman Candle Casting, a casting company recognized for assembling talent for major television and film projects.

Their involvement suggests The Woods will feature a carefully selected ensemble cast capable of delivering the emotional intensity and suspense that define Harlan Coben adaptations.

Why Harlan Coben Shows Continue to Dominate Netflix

Netflix’s partnership with Harlan Coben has become one of the streamer’s most successful ongoing collaborations.

Coben adaptations consistently perform well because they combine:

  • Fast-paced storytelling
  • Emotional drama
  • Shocking mysteries
  • Relatable characters
  • Binge-worthy suspense

With Michelle Keegan returning after the success of Fool Me Once, expectations are already high for The Woods.

Paradise TV Series: Cast, Plot, Casting Directors, and How to Get Cast

The hit post-apocalyptic thriller Paradise is quickly becoming one of the most talked-about shows in television. Created by Dan Fogelman and starring Sterling K. Brown, Julianne Nicholson, and James Marsden, the series blends political drama, mystery, and sci-fi into a gripping, binge-worthy experience.

Since its debut on Hulu in January 2025, Paradise has earned strong reviews, major award nominations, and a growing global fanbase. Here’s everything you need to know about the series—including the casting team behind it and how you can find similar opportunities.

What Is Paradise About?

Paradise is set inside a massive underground bunker in Colorado, three years after a devastating global event. The story follows Secret Service agent Xavier Collins as he investigates the murder of the President of the United States.

As Collins searches for answers, he becomes a suspect himself. His investigation reveals hidden conspiracies, powerful elites, and shocking truths about survival, trust, and control in a post-apocalyptic world.

Meet the Cast of Paradise

The show features an impressive cast delivering powerful performances:

  • Sterling K. Brown as Xavier Collins
  • Julianne Nicholson as Samantha “Sinatra” Redmond
  • James Marsden as President Cal Bradford
  • Sarah Shahi as Dr. Gabriela Torabi
  • Nicole Brydon Bloom as Agent Jane Driscoll
  • Krys Marshall as Agent Nicole Robinson
  • Enuka Okuma as Teri Rogers-Collins

Season 2 expands the cast with new characters played by Shailene Woodley, Thomas Doherty, and Michael McGrady.

Who Are the Casting Directors Behind Paradise?

Casting is a crucial part of what makes Paradise so compelling. The series features a highly experienced casting team responsible for assembling its talented ensemble.

Tiffany Little Canfield

Tiffany Little Canfield is a lead casting director on Paradise. She is known for her work on major productions like Wicked (2024), In the Heights (2021), and Margin Call (2011). Her ability to find emotionally authentic performers plays a big role in the show’s success.

Josh Einsohn

Production for Season 2 started in March 2025, with Season 3 already in development—showing long-term plans for the series.

Episodes are released in batches followed by weekly drops.

Prime Video’s Creed Spinoff Delphi Moves Toward Production

Prime Video is bringing the Creed spinoff Delphi to television, expanding one of Hollywood’s most recognizable boxing franchises into a new live-action drama series.

The upcoming series, titled Delphi, is set inside the fictional Delphi Boxing Academy, the Los Angeles gym closely connected to the Rocky and Creed film universes. The gym has served as an important training ground for both Apollo Creed and Adonis Creed, making it a meaningful setting for the next chapter of the franchise.

Prime Video announced the series order during Amazon’s annual upfront presentation in May 2025. While a premiere date has not yet been announced, the show is expected to follow a new group of young boxers as they train, compete, and fight for their futures inside the Delphi Boxing Academy.

What Is the Creed Spinoff Delphi About?

The Creed spinoff Delphi will focus on rising fighters training at the legendary Delphi Boxing Academy. In franchise canon, the gym was founded by Tony “Duke” Evers and later run by his son, Tony “Little Duke” Evers.

Fans of the Rocky and Creed films will recognize Delphi as more than just a boxing gym. It represents discipline, legacy, ambition, and the hard work required to become a champion. By centering the series around this location, Prime Video has the opportunity to explore new characters while staying connected to the emotional foundation of the Creed franchise.

Plot details remain under wraps, but Prime Video has described Delphi as the first live-action television extension of the Creed universe. The show is expected to introduce new fighters who will carry the franchise into a fresh era.

Michael B. Jordan Will Executive Produce Delphi

Michael B. Jordan, who stars as Adonis Creed in the Creed film trilogy, will executive produce the series through his Outlier Society banner alongside Liz Raposo.

Jordan has played a major role in shaping the modern Creed franchise, both in front of and behind the camera. His involvement in Delphi signals that the series will remain closely tied to the tone, themes, and legacy of the films.

Marco Ramírez will serve as showrunner and executive producer. Ramírez is known for his work on action-driven television dramas, including Netflix’s Daredevil and The Defenders. His experience with character-focused stories and intense physical worlds could make him a strong fit for a boxing drama set inside the Creed universe.

Irwin Winkler, David Winkler, and Charles Winkler will also executive produce for Winkler Films, the longtime production company behind the Rocky and Creed films.

Who Are the Casting Directors for Creed Spinoff Delphi?

Casting for Creed spinoff Delphi includes Alessi Hartigan Casting, one of the casting directors connected to the project.

Alessi Hartigan Casting is a well-known casting company with experience working on film, television, commercial, and background casting projects. Their involvement is especially important for performers who may be interested in future opportunities connected to the series.

Because Delphi is expected to follow young boxers training inside the fictional Delphi Boxing Academy, casting may include roles for actors, background performers, athletes, boxers, trainers, and talent with strong physical or sports-related experience.

Prime Video has not yet announced the main cast for Delphi, and additional casting details have not been fully released. However, the involvement of Alessi Hartigan Casting suggests that the production is continuing to move forward behind the scenes. As more updates become available, actors and entertainment professionals should monitor trusted casting platforms for verified opportunities.

Delphi Expands the Creed Universe on Prime Video

The Creed spinoff Delphi is part of a larger effort to build out the Creed franchise beyond feature films. Discussions between Michael B. Jordan’s Outlier Society and Amazon about expanding the Creed universe reportedly began roughly two years before the official series order.

Outlier Society currently has a first-look film deal and an overall television deal with Amazon MGM Studios. A separate Creed-related anime project has also been discussed, though it is not connected to Delphi.

The new series arrives as Amazon MGM Studios continues to develop streaming projects based on well-known MGM properties. Since Amazon’s acquisition of MGM, the studio has looked for ways to expand recognizable franchises for Prime Video audiences worldwide.

Why Delphi Could Be a Major Moment for Creed Fans

The Creed films have become a successful continuation of the Rocky franchise, introducing Adonis Creed as a new central figure while honoring the legacy of Apollo Creed and Rocky Balboa.

Across three films released in 2015, 2018, and 2023, the Creed franchise has built a strong audience with its mix of sports drama, family legacy, emotional storytelling, and high-stakes boxing action. A fourth Creed movie is also in development, meaning the franchise is continuing to grow across both film and television.

With Delphi, Prime Video can explore stories beyond Adonis Creed while still staying rooted in the world fans already know. The series may introduce new athletes, trainers, rivalries, and personal struggles, all connected by the legendary boxing gym at the center of the story.

Has the Delphi Cast Been Announced?

Prime Video has not yet announced the main cast for Delphi. A premiere date has also not been confirmed.

Because the series will follow young boxers training at Delphi Boxing Academy, future casting announcements could attract attention from actors, athletes, and performers with boxing, fitness, or stunt experience. As production moves forward, more information about casting, filming locations, and release plans is expected to emerge.

The Creed spinoff Delphi is shaping up to be an exciting new chapter for the Rocky and Creed universe. With Michael B. Jordan executive producing, Marco Ramírez leading the series, Prime Video backing the project, and Alessi Hartigan Casting connected to casting, Delphi could become a major new sports drama for streaming audiences.

Japanese Manga Adaptation “Bet” Renewed for Season 2 at Netflix After Global Top 10 Success

Netflix has officially renewed “Bet” for Season 2 following the show’s strong global performance and growing international fanbase.

The live-action series, inspired by the Japanese manga “Kakegurui,” quickly became one of Netflix’s standout teen dramas after its release. “Bet” spent three consecutive weeks in Netflix’s global Top 10 for English-language series, showing that the high-stakes boarding school drama connected with audiences around the world.

With its mix of psychological tension, elite school rivalry, underground gambling, and manga-inspired storytelling, “Bet” has become a major title to watch as Netflix continues expanding its lineup of international adaptations and teen-focused dramas.

What Is “Bet” About?

“Bet” is set at St. Dominic’s, an exclusive private academy where elite teens from around the world compete for enrollment, status, and power. However, St. Dominic’s is far from an ordinary boarding school.

At this prestigious institution, underground gambling determines the student hierarchy. A student’s social standing is shaped not by grades or popularity, but by their ability to win dangerous, high-pressure games. Those who succeed gain influence, while those who lose risk falling to the bottom of the school’s power structure.

The series follows Yumeko, played by Miku Martineau, a mysterious and exceptionally talented gambler whose arrival disrupts the school’s established order. With a shadowy past and a secret quest for revenge, Yumeko quickly becomes one of the most unpredictable forces at St. Dominic’s.

“Bet” Season 1 Introduced a World of Power, Risk, and Revenge

Season 1 of “Bet” followed Yumeko as she entered St. Dominic’s and began challenging the academy’s most powerful students. Her fearless approach to gambling and ability to read her opponents made her both a threat and a fascination to those around her.

As Yumeko took on increasingly dangerous games, the series explored themes of ambition, status, control, loyalty, and revenge. The show’s fast-paced storytelling, intense character dynamics, and stylish approach to the source material helped it stand out among Netflix’s teen dramas.

The success of “Bet” proves that audiences are continuing to respond to bold manga adaptations, especially when they combine suspense, strong visuals, and character-driven drama.

The Cast of “Bet”

Miku Martineau leads “Bet” as Yumeko. She is known for her work in “Kate” and “Star Trek: Section 31.”

The ensemble cast also includes:

Eve Edwards

Clara Alexandrova

Hunter Cardinal

Anwen O’Driscoll

Aviva Mongillo

Dorian Giordano

Emma Elle Paterson

Peter Outerbridge

With “Bet” renewed for Season 2, fans can expect the series to return to the world of St. Dominic’s for more gambling, rivalry, and dramatic twists.

Who Are the Casting Directors for “Bet”?

The casting team behind “Bet” played an important role in bringing the high-stakes world of St. Dominic’s to life. A series like “Bet” depends on a strong ensemble cast that can deliver intensity, mystery, competition, and emotional depth.

According to the project’s casting credits, Maureen Evans is listed as a casting director for “Bet.” Evans is a casting professional known for work on projects such as “Cube Zero,” “The Office Movers,” and “FUBAR.” Her casting work helped support the show’s ensemble-driven storytelling and contributed to finding performers who could match the tone of the series.

Jade Hesson is also credited in the casting department as additional crew. Hesson is associated with Larissa Mair Casting & Associates and has experience supporting casting efforts for film and television productions. Casting assistants and additional casting crew members often help with talent organization, audition coordination, and the overall casting process.

In addition, Twins Talent Agency is also connected to the casting team for this project. Talent agencies and casting professionals help connect productions with performers who fit the needs of each role, making them a key part of the production process.

Together, the casting team helped shape the cast of “Bet,” contributing to the performances and ensemble dynamic that helped the series reach global audiences.

Simon Barry Developed “Bet” for Netflix

Director and showrunner Simon Barry developed “Bet” for television based on “Kakegurui,” the popular Japanese manga series created by writer Homura Kawamoto and illustrator Tōru Naomura.

Barry celebrated the renewal by sharing excitement for the show’s fans around the world and for the cast and crew returning to St. Dominic’s for more gambling and chaos.

The series is executive produced by Barry, Jeff F. King, David Fortier, Ivan Schneeberg, Jon Rutherford, and Nick Nantell. Boat Rocker serves as the production company behind the series.

“Bet” Is Inspired by the Japanese Manga “Kakegurui”

“Bet” is based on “Kakegurui,” which means “compulsive gambler.” The manga debuted in 2014 and was created by writer Homura Kawamoto and illustrator Tōru Naomura.

Since its launch, the source material has built a loyal fanbase and expanded across multiple volumes. Known for its psychological tension, dramatic gambling battles, and school-based power struggles, “Kakegurui” provided the foundation for Netflix’s live-action adaptation.

The Netflix version of “Bet” reimagines the story for a global audience while keeping the core concept of students battling for power through gambling.

What to Expect From “Bet” Season 2

Netflix has not yet revealed full plot details for “Bet” Season 2, but the renewal confirms that Yumeko’s story at St. Dominic’s is far from over.

Fans can likely expect more dangerous games, shifting alliances, hidden secrets, and intense rivalries as the academy’s power structure continues to evolve. With Yumeko already shaking up the school, Season 2 could raise the stakes even higher.

The renewal also highlights the continued success of manga-inspired stories on global streaming platforms. As audiences continue embracing international adaptations, “Bet” could become an even bigger title for Netflix in its second season.

Why the “Bet” Renewal Matters

The renewal of “Bet” is a major sign that manga adaptations and international teen dramas remain in demand. Netflix’s decision to move forward with Season 2 reflects the show’s strong viewership and its ability to connect with audiences worldwide.

For fans, the renewal means more episodes, more gambling, and more secrets from St. Dominic’s.
